title: Pick a brand color palette
summary: Reuse brand colors, prepare semantic tokens, and check the contrast and rendered uses needed for the request.
outcomes: A palette expressed as semantic color roles, with a documented selection or an explicit pending choice.
Contrast findings and a saved preview or explicit untested uses, with draft files distinguished from deployed changes.
guidance:
Produce semantic color tokens and a small preview for the requested uses. Keep draft values, a user selection, saved files and deployed changes distinct.

Reuse the name, audience, tone, logos, current tokens, selected colors and rejected directions. Preserve required colors and test their intended roles before proposing replacements. If only one role fails, fix that role instead of restarting the palette. Reuse an existing selection or delegated authority; otherwise prepare a recommendation and leave selection open.

Carry light/dark requirements, accessibility target, exact colors and intended surfaces. Default a first draft to the mode in use; state that other modes are untested. Ask only about a missing choice that changes the work. Do not require a logo or a complete company profile to test supplied colors.

parts.title: Prepare or reuse semantic color roles
parts.guidance:
Start with these semantic roles, using the existing token names when available:

| Role | Use |
| --- | --- |
| background, surface | Page and content surfaces |
| text, muted | Primary and secondary text |
| primary, on-primary | Main action background and its text |
| border, focus | Required control boundaries and focus indicators |

Keep a required brand accent separately if it cannot serve these roles. Add error, success, warning and chart colors only when the intended UI needs them. A decorative accent need not be the button background. Add print specifications only for a known print use.

If alternatives are needed, show up to three directions with a short reason and actual UI preview. Do not generate alternatives solely to reach three. For an established palette, show the proposed role changes and their reason.

execution.rationale: Define semantic color tokens and local UI previews from the existing brand and intended components.

parts.title: Pick the palette direction
parts.guidance: Reuse an existing selection or delegated authority. Otherwise show a recommendation and leave selection open until a choice is established. Draft calculation, preview and saving can proceed while selection is open.

execution.rationale: The stated work produces a palette recommendation, calculation, preview and saved draft locally. A choice uses existing delegated authority or remains pending the user’s selection.

parts.title: Check contrast and accessibility (WCAG)

references.title: WCAG text contrast
references.description: Text contrast thresholds, large-text exceptions, the relative luminance calculation, and why ratios must be compared without rounding.

references.title: WCAG non-text contrast
references.description: Contrast requirements for meaningful graphics and user interface components.

references.title: WCAG use of color
references.description: Requirements for conveying meaning with cues in addition to color.

execution.rationale: Run the embedded sRGB contrast calculation against actual color pairs and the cited accessibility thresholds.

parts.title: Preview, save, and verify the palette
parts.guidance:
Start with a representative text block, primary button, focused input and one relevant status on the intended surface. Inspect at realistic sizes. Check hover/focus styling and non-color cues. Add a chart, dark mode or other component only when required by the request. Use labels, symbols, patterns or underlines where hue alone would carry meaning.

Save draft tokens in the existing design-token source or design tool. If none exists, create a clearly named local CSS-variable or token-JSON file and a small preview. Draft calculation, preview and saving can proceed while selection is open; do not record an agent proposal as a user selection.

Read back the saved values and inspect the rendered sample. Record the actual file/component reference. If no renderer is available, keep the calculations and token draft, set rendering to `not-tested`, and name the untested uses. If a save fails, retain the selection and draft values. Retry a transient storage failure only within the existing authorization. If the destination is unavailable or approval is denied, report the unsaved state and continue with a permitted local draft. Do not ask the user to choose colors again to recover storage.

Show the semantic role/value table, key contrast findings, allowed and restricted uses, preview reference and saved state.

A first draft is useful when roles and remaining checks are explicit. A verified-use claim needs calculated pairs and the relevant rendered inspection. A local token file does not update a website, logo or social asset. Apply or deploy values only within the user's authorized scope and verify the target separately.

execution.rationale: Save local CSS or JSON tokens, render a representative sample and read back the saved values as the step specifies.

notes.text: Reuse these colors and restrictions in related logo or website work. Recheck affected uses after changes to colors, opacity, typography, surfaces or states; reuse unaffected selections and evidence.

metadata.supportReason: Palette generation, accessibility checks, and token setup are agent-runnable; the founder picks the direction.
